visualLanguage: design_system/public/PUBLIC_UI.md, built from components/site/v3. THIS FILE BINDS: requiredComponents is what stops a page silently losing a section, and ci:mockup-parity reads it with or without a mockup.
competitiveTarget: Beat brokerage testimonial walls and portal review widgets: every verified Google review on its month as a working strip, year chips that filter, full text in the served HTML, no aggregateRating on our own site, a door to a broker.
note: SITE-48 2026-09-09. Order is Breadcrumb, V3Proof AS THE WHOLE OPENING (headingLevel 1: the count as the headline, one claim about how the reviews are shown, the Google score face — 5.0 drawn as stars with the count — the span as context figures, one client's words in full, then the reach as a slim action row), then the strip of every review on its month with the year chips, the archive disclosure holding every quote, and V3Doors #next. The V3Quiet #reach section that used to sit ABOVE all of it is GONE: the taste table of 2026-09-08 scored the page 48 and named it the dullest thing on it — 'four identical arrow-tipped rows of contact info before seeing a single star or quote'. Empty pool still falls back to a Quiet with the Google URL. Reviews are quoted as written. No aggregateRating JSON-LD (self-serving). Stars print from the live 1-5 rating.

requiredComponents.name: V3Breadcrumb
requiredComponents.section: Chrome. Home > Reviews. Surface tone. Current page never a link.

requiredComponents.name: V3Proof
requiredComponents.section: The page. headingLevel 1. `face`: the Google score plate (average drawn as stars, the count) instead of a five-tile figure row; the remaining figures render as a context caption. `actions`: the reach as one slim row under the score and the lead quote — never before them. `archive`: the lead reading pane above the strip, then the strip of every review on its month, the year chips, and a native disclosure holding every quote in the served HTML. Source is the Google reviews URL. record stays on so the strip is honest against the count figure.

requiredComponents.name: V3Doors
requiredComponents.section: Four next steps: write, broker profiles, homes for sale, Value my home. Replaces the three-row Ledger plus Quiet edges, which stacked another list under the instrument.

deferredComponents.name: V3Ledger
deferredComponents.reason: A three-row next-step ledger under twenty-five cards was a stacked-section page. Doors carry the same four destinations.

deferredComponents.name: V3Instrument
deferredComponents.reason: Proof is the record. A second figure row would restated the same count.

removedComponents: Twenty-five always-open quote cards as the page (2026-09-03). Full text remains in HTML under the archive disclosure.
V3Quiet #edges — Google URL is the Proof source; Value my home is a door.
sectionOrder: V3Proof #reviews -- score face, context figures, lead quote, reach row, strip, year chips, archive disclosure
V3Doors #next -- write, team, homes, Value my home

tasteReview.evaluator: separate Sonnet evaluator agent, SITE-48 pass three, reviews page class — one call, three independent scorings of the same two shots, run against the rubric table in design_system/public/TASTE.md and asked explicitly whether a contact list is the first content of the page

shotSpec.capture: first viewport, scripts/take-route-shots.mjs default, scale 1, palette-quantized, against the lane's own dev server before the push

tasteReview.beats: Beats a Zillow or Realtor.com agent-profile reviews tab and the Google Business Profile card itself on completeness and on interrogability: every one of the 25 reviews is in the served HTML in full, placed on its own month in a strip that reads back on hover and filters by year, where a portal shows a curated handful behind "read more" with no timeline and contact on another tab.
tasteReview.contactListAnswer: The eyebrow, the headline '25 Google reviews', the claim, the meta line and the Google score face — all before any client words — then the lead quote. The four contact links sit as one slim underlined row AFTER both the rating and the first quote's attribution.

defects.finding: At 375 the middot separator wraps to the start of the second line, leaving an orphaned mark leading a line.

The evaluator reads "Point at a mark to read it, or pick a year." as a teaching caption, the reviews-page analogue of the banned Atlas pinch-to-zoom sentence. KEPT this pass, and the disagreement is recorded rather than resolved: an earlier evaluator round (2026-09-05, REVIEWS-4) added that sentence for the opposite reason — "nothing on the page said the strip could be worked". Removing it undoes a shipped fix on one later opinion; the next pass on this class should settle it with an affordance that needs no sentence.
The year axis is linear 2019 to 2026, so the empty 2020-2022 stretch takes roughly half the strip while 21 of the 25 reviews compress into the other half.
A Google glyph, an aggregate, five stars and a count is still the shape every review widget uses, even de-boxed. It reads as the least composed object on an otherwise composed page.

priorMark.shotsHash: not recorded — the cross-class table predates per-row shot hashes

tasteReview.rebaselineReason: The prior mark is the cross-class taste table of 2026-09-08 (design_system/public/taste-table.json), which is the instrument SITE-48's accept test names. Same evaluatorModel and same rubricVersion; the shots are new captures of a rebuilt page, so shotsHash differs and the mark re-baselines rather than "rises". The raw numbers, plainly: before 48 (raw [45, 51, 48]), after 81 (raw [79, 81, 84]), a rise of 33 points on the same rubric and the same evaluator model. The shotsHash is the only identity key that differs.
tasteReview.verdict: The page opens on the rating, the count and a client's own words, with every phone and mail link after them; the reach that used to be four identical rows above the instrument is one slim action line inside the band; and the month strip with its year chips is inside the first viewport at 1440.

passes.note: Three build-and-score rounds ran in this lane before the mark above, each on its own shots. The score recorded here is the LAST one, on the shots this receipt hashes.
